item.text: {"analysis":"The convolutional trial completed successfully but achieved macro validation HR@10 of 0.4987, below the supplied 0.505 baseline by 0.0063. Category HR@10 was 0.575 for Movies_and_TV, 0.555 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.360 for Electronics, and 0.505 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics had the lowest absolute performance; category-specific baseline scores were not supplied, so relative gains or regressions cannot be assigned by category. These results do not support an overall improvement from this convolutional hypothesis. They do not establish whether limited motif structure, optimization, or regularization caused the shortfall; training curves and selected epochs were not provided. Allocated GPU time was 311.69 seconds.","code_summary":"One independently trained causal convolutional network per category, with 96-dimensional tied input/output item embeddings, learned item biases, maximum history length 64, and four residual blocks with dilations 1, 2, 4, and 8. Each block contains two causal width-3 convolutions, LayerNorm, GELU, and dropout 0.25. Training uses sampled next-item cross-entropy with 256 shared uniform negatives, at most 2,048 target positions per batch, AdamW, learning-rate warmup and cosine decay, and gradient clipping. Random prefix windows mix terminal and earlier transitions. Validation HR@10 selects exactly one checkpoint per category. The generated predictor reconstructs the same architecture and routes each dataset to its single selected model; no ensemble or separately fitted scoring component is used."}
